acceptedAnswer.text: A phishing simulation is a controlled exercise that emulates phishing attacks to measure employee response, reporting behaviour, and SOC readiness without exposing the organisation to real-world risk.

mainEntity.name: Are these simulations safe and legally compliant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Phishing simulations operate under a Rules of Engagement (ROE) reviewed with stakeholders and legal counsel. Sensitive employees can be excluded and evidence is handled securely.

mainEntity.name: How frequently should we run simulations?

acceptedAnswer.text: Monthly micro-campaigns are recommended as part of continuous programs, with quarterly comprehensive reporting. Frequency can be adjusted based on risk cohorts.

mainEntity.name: Will employees be penalised for failing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our recommended approach focuses on coaching and targeted training, not punitive actions. Organisations may choose to define their own HR policies separately.
Yes, remediation includes role-based micro-learning content, quizzes, and LMS-integrated training modules to address identified weaknesses.
Yes. Credential harvesting simulations are conducted on isolated, encrypted endpoints with immediate containment and no storage of plaintext credentials.
Yes. Voice phishing (vishing) and SMS phishing (smishing) simulations are available to assess mobile and communication-channel risks.

mainEntity.name: Can you target specific departments or geographies?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, campaigns can be segmented by role, business unit, or geography to align with specific policy constraints and risk focus areas.
Results are shared via executive summaries, technical evidence packs, and an interactive dashboard accessible to authorised users.
Key KPIs include click-through rate (CTR), report rate, susceptibility index, repeat failures, mean time to detect (MTTD) for simulated incidents, and training remediation completion.
Onboarding typically takes 1-2 weeks for pilots and 2-4 weeks for larger rollouts, depending on integrations and organisational approvals.

mainEntity.name: Do you integrate with SIEM, LMS, or HR systems?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Integrations are available through connectors and APIs, allowing simulated events to be forwarded to SIEMs, training tasks to be assigned via LMS, and users mapped through HR systems.
Yes. All personal data is protected with contractual safeguards, encryption in transit and at rest, and data retention policies agreed with clients.

mainEntity.name: Does phishing simulation help with compliance?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Deliverables include compliance mapping for ISO 27001, SOC 2, and privacy frameworks, supporting audits and certifications.
You can contact ISECURION at info@isecurion.com or submit the enquiry form on the website. A discovery call will be scheduled, followed by an SOW and timeline.

mainEntity.name: What is a good phishing click-through rate benchmark?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mature security-aware organisations typically target a click-through rate below 5%, with continuous monthly simulation programs used to track progress toward that benchmark over time.

mainEntity.name: How is phishing simulation different from a real phishing attack?

acceptedAnswer.text: Phishing simulation uses the same lure techniques as real attackers but runs under an agreed Rules of Engagement, with no data exfiltration, safe credential capture, opt-out lists for sensitive staff, and immediate containment of any accidental exposure.
